source: CARDI book "ដំណាំស្រូវនៅកម្ពុជា" (Rice Cultivation in Cambodia), by Men Sarom, Thuy Lina and Pheng Thimuny, published by CARDI, 2007, Chapter 11 (Economics and market), including a regional comparison table (Table 11.9) and discussion of Green Revolution variety adoption. No elibrary URL visible.
text: This source situates Cambodia's rice sector within a wider Southeast Asian context. A comparison table covers rice area, yield, and production across three time periods (1961-1970, 1985-1990, and 2001-2004) for Cambodia and neighboring/regional producers (Thailand, Vietnam, Myanmar, Laos, the Philippines, Indonesia, and Malaysia), illustrating that Cambodia's production growth over this span, while substantial, followed a different trajectory than Vietnam's especially rapid growth over the same period (Vietnam's rise is attributed partly to earlier and more extensive adoption of Green Revolution semi-dwarf varieties and irrigation investment). On variety impact specifically, the source traces the regional impact of IRRI's IR-series varieties: IR8 (the original 'miracle rice' of the 1960s Green Revolution) was succeeded by improved lines IR36, IR64, and IR72, each with better disease/pest resistance and grain quality than its predecessor, and adoption of these lines (or Cambodia's own CARDI-bred varieties drawing on similar breeding lineage) is credited with meaningful yield gains where used, especially in irrigated dry-season conditions (Hossain, 1996; Greenland, 1997). On market/pricing, the source notes that traditional, aromatic, and higher-grain-quality varieties command a price premium over high-yielding modern varieties in local and export markets, meaning farmers face a real trade-off between raw yield and market price per kilogram when choosing what to grow.
caveat: The regional comparison table's exact figures were not transcribed in detail here given the dense multi-country, multi-period table format; the qualitative trend (Cambodia's growth trajectory relative to Vietnam and other regional producers) is presented instead. Recommend a duplicate-check against Batch 18's national area/production history content, which covers Cambodia's own trajectory in more numeric detail from a different chapter of this same book.
